facts.text: Manning was named for the Manning family, who produced three South Carolina governors, including John Laurence Manning.
The Old Manning Library, built in 1908, features an unusual octagonal interior and a high domed skylight, the only building in town on the National Register.
A bronze statue of “Amelia Bedelia,” the beloved children’s character created by local author Peggy Parish, greets visitors outside the Harvin‑Clarendon County Public Library.
Manning’s climate is humid subtropical, with hot, humid summers and mild winters, averaging 75.2°F highs and 52.4°F lows.
Railroads, abundant timber, and diverse agriculture helped Manning flourish in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
In 1960, Manning joined other Southern towns in staging peaceful civil‑rights demonstrations and sit‑ins, marking a pivotal moment in the movement.
